name: Cimbáeth
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.

attributes.attribute: one of three Ulster kings who ruled in turn
second king of the pact who died in battle
third king who opposed Macha and was killed
daughter of Áed Ruad who took his turn and wed Cimbáeth

text: Cimbáeth was an Irish hero. With two other kings of Ulster, Áed Ruad and Díthorba, he agreed that each man would govern a seven year turn. A council of poets, nobles, and druids watched over the pact. The rotation held until Áed died. His daughter Macha Mong Rua then claimed his turn. Cimbáeth and Díthorba refused her and met her in war. Macha carried the day. She married Cimbáeth and cut down Díthorba.

okr.objective: Cimbáeth shared the throne of Ulster under a pact of rotation with two fellow kings.
key_results: Cimbáeth agreed with Áed Ruad and Díthorba to rule in turns of seven years.
After Áed died, Macha Mong Rua took his turn by force.
Macha won the battle, married Cimbáeth, and slew Díthorba.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
